text.p: Finnish insurer Pohjola is expected to show an operating profit of 507.5 million markka for the first six months of 1997, a Reuter poll showed on Monday.
The results are due on August 21 at 0630 GMT. In 1996, Pohjola's January-June operating profit was 466 million markka.
In March, Pohjola said it expected higher premium income in 1997, but the balance on the technical account would not change markedly from 1996.

Five analysts polled gave forecasts for full-year 1997, and the median was for a 750 million markka operating profit (mean 751). Estimates ranged from 510 to 1,025 million markka, and analysts said it was difficult to estimate how the insurer would book securities gains.
In 1996 Pohjola's full-year operating profit was 526 million markka.
Contributing to the survey were Aros Securities, Alfred Berg, Carnegie, Evli Securities, Handelsbanken and Merita.
